key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with microscopy plus machine-learning image analysis.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a fast, non-invasive screening workflow to flag unstable perovskite films before device fabrication, supporting more reliable scale-up of solar cells.
method: nano-FTIR to chemically identify impurity phases
high-resolution reflected light microscopy for rapid imaging
machine-learning-supported image analysis to quantify impurity density
evidence_signal: Photo-stress and degradation tracking showed that failure starts at impurity–perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded faster in early-stage testing.
watch_item: The screening is chemically validated, but deployment will still depend on robust calibration across film compositions, imaging conditions, and manufacturing lines.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
